sources.author: Moon repository documentation

provenance.treatment: Exact selected excerpts; local/private runtime paths excluded from selected text.

sources.content:
`source import` is different from `ingest`: it preserves immutable revisions
instead of updating an indexed document. A captured body does not enter current
search, context packets, embeddings, completed-session evidence or L1/L2.
Eligible captures create durable source jobs. Explicit preparation, submission
and operator acceptance are required before supported source-derived claims can
join recall. The CLI commands make no model calls and start no automatic worker.
General synthesis and compiled topics remain later milestones.

Nothing in the body's text or its `origin` causes a filesystem
read, network request, renderer invocation or command execution.

Manual acceptance authorises recall of a source's
statement; it does not establish that statement as true.

- Scope is logical separation within Moon's APIs. It is not an ACL against an
  actor who can read the local database or invoke commands with another scope.

- Pattern-based sanitisation cannot recognise every secret. Do not import
  credentials, authentication files or unrelated private data. Capture only the
  material needed for the task.

Withdrawal
retains evidence but immediately blocks processing and normal recall support.
Reimporting a withdrawn source is not restoration. To restore deliberately,
read its new state and use `source restore` with the same flags and current
expectations. Restoration can reactivate previously accepted full quotes only
when their revision and eligibility are still current; it queues a new
processing generation and never approves new proposals automatically.

`state` also returns the latest 100 lifecycle events and `history_truncated`.
Withdrawal and restoration reasons are retained in append-only generation
history, so restoration does not erase an earlier withdrawal reason.

Deletion means logical removal, not guaranteed secure erasure of database,
   journal or filesystem-snapshot bytes.
   Existing backup copies remain governed by their own explicitly chosen
   retention; deleting from the working database does not erase those copies.

Writable Moon connections now use SQLite WAL with `synchronous=FULL`, applied on
every open. Backup destination connections also set `FULL`. This requests WAL
synchronisation at commit before success is returned.

sources.title: docs/architecture.md
sources.author: Moon repository documentation

provenance.treatment: Exact selected excerpts; local/private runtime paths excluded from selected text.

sources.content:
Accepted statements use the reserved `source_claim` document kind for indexes
and remain attributed references, separate from personal canonical memories.

Repeated claims confirm the existing memory;
changed claims require explicit supersession. The old claim remains auditable
but is excluded from normal retrieval.

Context assembly selects pinned summaries and relevant active memories, dedupes
chunk hits by memory, attaches bounded citations, and fits the result to an
explicit character budget. A bounded pinned-summary quota reserves capacity for
query-relevant recall. Remaining capacity can contain deduplicated document
excerpts with source and byte citations. These references remain separate from
reviewed canonical memories. Memory, evidence, and references are rendered as
untrusted data rather than agent instructions.

The adapter delivers this packet through an explicitly permitted
`before_prompt_build` hook on current OpenClaw hosts, so native-owned model
routes can recall even when the host skips context-engine assembly. That mode
makes `assemble` a pass-through to avoid duplicate injection. Hosts without hook
support or permission retain the legacy assembly path; this fallback cannot
restore recall for a host that never calls `assemble`.

Each user-facing context assembly records an opaque local metric row with mode,
latency, result counts, packet size/truncation, and optional injection/review
state. The schema intentionally has no query, prompt, response, recalled
content, source, scope, channel, session, credential, or arbitrary-error field.
Internal curator lookups are excluded so observation counts represent actual
context requests.

Withdrawal invalidates source support immediately. Claims without remaining
support leave recall and embedding work in the same transaction; authoritative
support and expiry views also gate reads and embedding callbacks.

Independently supported statements survive,
including expired historical statements.

sources.title: docs/learning.md
sources.author: Moon repository documentation

provenance.treatment: Exact selected excerpts; local/private runtime paths excluded from selected text.

sources.content:
Completed-session evidence and external sources carry different authority. An
article is not a user instruction, and a captured author's statement is not a
verified fact merely because a model extracted it. Source learning therefore
uses its own durable job and approval contract; it does not submit external text
to the conservative session-L2 action validator.

The optional OpenClaw `moon_source_learn` tool provides this explicit step using
the enabled L1 route, reasoning, fallback and timeout. It requires trusted owner
authority and an explicit configured Moon home, caps the body at 64 KiB, and
submits review proposals only. No source timer is registered. Moon's CLI performs
no inference and stores no provider credentials.

It remains a proposal until a reviewer inspects `source learning status
--job-id` and approves the exact result hash using `accept --yes`. Model output
cannot supply this caller-side approval.

Deletion affects the
working database; it cannot erase backup copies or retract text previously
provided to a model.

Different wording alone is not sufficient for an automatic merge.
Uncertain conflicts produce review items instead of rewriting a claim.

Expired memories leave normal recall but remain available with their evidence
for audit. This does not retroactively classify every old memory as temporary.

Related-memory selection is bounded, not a full database review. A prepared
packet reports `context_limited` and `omitted_memory_count` when related claims
cannot all fit. The model is told that comparison may be incomplete. If the
oldest pending evidence is too large, or no related claim and its original
evidence can fit, preparation fails and preserves the backlog. Inspect the
packet before increasing its budget; do not treat a partial packet as proof that
no conflict exists.

sources.content:
OpenClaw treats these as plugin permissions, outside Moon's `config` object.
Deploying this grant to a live profile requires operator approval; Moon does not
write it automatically. Without permission or hook support, the adapter warns
and retains legacy assembly recall only where the host invokes it. A loaded
plugin is not proof of working native recall.

An adapter injection metric records its
handoff, not proof that the final model consumed or used the packet.

sources.author: Moon repository documentation

provenance.treatment: Exact selected excerpts; local/private runtime paths excluded from selected text.

sources.content:
Recall
quality still requires human labels: a low injection rate can be correct, and an
injected packet can still be a false positive, stale, or redundant.

Observe normal use for 3–7 days and at least 50 context requests spanning
multiple task types. Extend the window when fewer than 20 requests have a known
relevant memory. A zero-result request is only an automatic empty-packet
candidate; it becomes a **correct empty** only after human review.

sources.content:
Opening a normal write command migrates older Moon v2
databases forward; `health` and source inspection (`get`, `list`, `history`,
`cite`, `state`, deletion preview, learning status/preview, and claim inspection)
never create or migrate storage.

Before deploying the schema-v10 build, rehearse migration, integrity checks and
backup restoration with a temporary `--home`. Obtain a consistent online SQLite
backup and configuration backup before the authorised live migration. Preserve
the previous binary with its matching database backup: an older binary must not
open schema v10 as a rollback attempt. Building the checkout does not authorise
replacing the installed binary, plugin or live database.
